judgements.reason: OneParameterSemigroups is essentially finished in the baseline: hilleYosida_generation_iff, the Lumer-Phillips iff, hausdorff_bernstein_widder, TauCeti.bochner and bcr_semigroup_bochner are all present, leaving only the complexified resolvent, Stieltjes converses and the Stone/LCA stretches. HopfRinow still has no exponential map at all, and needs C^k dependence of ODE solutions, the geodesic flow, normal neighbourhoods and the Gauss lemma before the Hopf-Rinow TFAE can even be stated.

KTheoryLowDegrees must build stable GL(A)/E(A) and K1 with Whitehead's lemma, the stable determinant and SK1, Bass-Milnor-Serre for S-integers, lambda-operations and det : K0 -> Pic, K0 of curves, and on top of that its U.6/Z.6 comparisons import BGL(A)+ and pi_0 K, i.e. the higher K-theory that neither library has. HopfRinow is much further along - Layer 0 and the connection/spray half of Layer 1 are built - and its remaining work is the exponential map, the Gauss lemma and the Hopf-Rinow TFAE, with no imports from other roadmaps.

CFSG already has thirteen of seventeen Lie-type carriers plus all twenty-six sporadic presentations, so its blocking work is the 3D4 triality carrier, the short-root G2/F4 group schemes with their special isogenies, and the uniform assembly; L5's Chevalley-Demazure import is large but the roadmap says A0 does not wait on it. KTheoryLowDegrees has ten of twelve layers unbuilt - all of K1 and its calculus, Bass-Milnor-Serre, exterior powers and det : K0 -> Pic, K0 of curves - and additionally imports the plus construction and pi_0 K, which do not exist.

LocallyAnalyticDistributions has none of its five layers built and must start from non-archimedean locally convex/LF topologies, which neither library has, then stack C^la spaces, the unbounded Amice transform, Vishik uniqueness, rigid character spaces and Fredholm/slope theory. CFSG is six of nine layers built and needs only four remaining Lie-type branches plus assembly on top of an already-large built base, even counting L5's Chevalley-Demazure obligation.

ArithmeticDynamics needs polarized morphisms with ample line bundles, a whole Berkovich analytic geometry with metrized line bundles and local measures, arithmetic equidistribution, dynatomic schemes and arboreal Galois representations, drawing on thirteen upstream roadmaps - 'Berkovich', 'dynatomic' and 'arboreal' have zero occurrences in the baseline. LocallyAnalyticDistributions is p-adic functional analysis over a single upstream roadmap, and Mathlib already supplies Mahler's theorem and the bounded Amice transform it extends.

Both need a non-archimedean analytic layer, but ArithmeticDynamics needs the wider one - Berkovich spectra, model metrics, semipositive metrized line bundles and local measures - plus ample line bundles and polarized morphisms, arithmetic equidistribution, dynatomic schemes and arboreal Galois representations, across thirteen upstream roadmaps. ColemanIntegration is heavy in one direction (Frobenius lifts on good-reduction curves, rigid/de Rham cohomology, Coleman functions and p-adic polylogarithms, on top of the unbounded Amice transform), but its upstream closure is a third the size.

ArithmeticLocallySymmetricSpaces must build Cartan involutions and symmetric spaces of real reductive groups, adelic reduction theory, the Borel-Serre compactification as a manifold with corners, derived Hecke correspondences and Poincare-Lefschetz duality with local coefficients - and neither library has a cup product or any Poincare duality. ColemanIntegration's stack, rigid/de Rham cohomology of curves with Frobenius continuation plus the unbounded Amice transform and p-adic L-functions, runs to six upstream roadmaps against fourteen.

Both are large, but GeneralAlgebraicKTheory is one tower on a real foundation: Mathlib already supplies SimplicialSet, nerve, ModelCategory, SingularHomology and homotopy groups, and Tau Ceti supplies ExactStructure and ExactK0, so three of its layers are partly built. ArithmeticLocallySymmetricSpaces has none of its eight layers built and needs several independent unbuilt towers - symmetric spaces and maximal compacts, adelic reduction theory, Borel-Serre corners, cup products and Poincare-Lefschetz duality with local coefficients - at BFS depth eight across fourteen upstream roadmaps.

BorelRegulators' upstream closure all but contains GeneralAlgebraicKTheory's (only three of its stages lie outside), and then adds ArithmeticKTheory's finite generation of K_n(O_F), Borel-Serre models, relative Lie-algebra cohomology and van Est, the stable cohomology of compact duals, and the continuation and functional equation of zeta_F with its order of vanishing. GeneralAlgebraicKTheory stops at the K-theory spectrum itself.

AutomorphicGaloisRepresentations needs modular curves and Jacobians as schemes, Kuga-Sato varieties, etale cohomology with local systems, Eichler-Shimura, Weil-II purity, local Langlands for GL2, Hilbert modular varieties and the Fontaine functors - fifty upstream roadmaps at depth fourteen, none of it present. BorelRegulators' tower, higher K-theory plus Borel-Serre plus Lie-algebra cohomology plus zeta_F, is twenty upstream roadmaps at depth nine.

AutomorphicGaloisRepresentations' upstream closure adds twenty-eight roadmaps that HodgeTate never needs - ModularCurvesPartII, DeligneWeightsAndPurity, DiamondEtaleCohomology, SmoothRepresentationsOfLocalGroups, GL2 transfer, endoscopic trace comparison - i.e. modular curves and Jacobians, Weil-II purity and local Langlands, on top of most of the perfectoid/adic stack HodgeTate uses. HodgeTate needs beyond it only AutomorphicBundles, a little more PerfectoidSpaces and its own log-adic and canonical-subgroup layers.

SerreWeightAndLevelOptimisation sits on all of AutomorphicGaloisRepresentations - which already strictly dominates HodgeTate's closure - and then adds finite flat group schemes and integral p-adic Hodge theory, Neron models and character groups, integral Hecke modules and mod-p forms, Mazur's principle and Ribet's level lowering, and Edixhoven's weight theorem. HodgeTate's own perfectoid, canonical-subgroup and logarithmic period work is large but is a proper part of that stack plus its own seven layers.

ShimuraCompactifications' entire upstream closure lies inside SerreWeightAndLevelOptimisation's on all but four stages, so Serre weight needs everything toroidal compactification needs and then modular curves with bad-reduction integral models, etale cohomology and Galois representations attached to forms, finite flat group schemes, Neron models, and the level-lowering and weight theorems themselves. ShimuraCompactifications stops at the toroidal geometry and its degeneration data.

ShimuraCompactifications must first have Shimura data, Shimura varieties with canonical models, abelian schemes and PEL moduli - none of which exists in either library - and then build arithmetic fans, analytic gluing, Mumford-Faltings-Chai degeneration and integral compactifications, across twenty-three upstream roadmaps at depth twelve. ColemanIntegration needs rigid/de Rham cohomology of good-reduction curves, Frobenius continuation, Coleman functions and p-adic polylogarithms, over six upstream roadmaps.

ArithmeticDynamics has five of seven layers unbuilt and no vocabulary in the baseline for Berkovich spaces, dynatomic schemes, equidistribution or arboreal representations; it must import scheme and moduli foundations, the height machine, Berkovich analytic geometry with metrized line bundles, and arithmetic fundamental groups. CFSG is six of nine layers built, with thirteen of seventeen Lie-type carriers and all twenty-six sporadic presentations already in Tau Ceti, leaving four branches, the uniform assembly and L5.

SerreWeightAndLevelOptimisation's closure is over three times the size (fifty-one upstream roadmaps at depth seventeen against twenty at depth nine) and includes the whole modular-curve, etale-cohomology, local-Langlands and p-adic-Hodge stack behind Galois representations attached to modular forms, plus finite flat group schemes, Neron models and the level-lowering and weight theorems. BorelRegulators needs a comparably tall but narrower tower - higher K-theory, Borel-Serre models, relative Lie-algebra cohomology and the functional equation of zeta_F.

ShimuraCompactifications' upstream closure is a strict subset of HodgeTate's - HodgeTate lists it as a prerequisite and consumes C3, C4 and C6 - so HodgeTate needs all the toroidal geometry and then perfectoid spaces, diamonds, pro-etale and log adic sites, p-divisible groups, relative period sheaves, canonical subgroups with quantitative bounds and Igusa towers. None of those objects exists in either library.

LocallyAnalyticDistributions has none of its five layers built and must first create non-archimedean locally convex and LF topologies, then stack C^la spaces and their duals, the unbounded Amice transform, Vishik uniqueness, rigid character spaces with the Mellin transform, and Fredholm determinants with slope decompositions, on top of an upstream roadmap that is itself only partly built. HopfRinow has Layer 0 and the Levi-Civita/spray part of Layer 1 in the baseline and needs three further layers - ODE smooth dependence and the exponential map, the Gauss lemma and minimisation, and the TFAE - with no imports.

GeneralAlgebraicKTheory consumes KTheoryLowDegrees' U.1 and Z.1 and then must build everything above degree zero: the Q-construction and K_n = pi_{n+1}|NQ(C)|, the plus construction, additivity, devissage, resolution and localisation, Waldhausen's S-construction with delooping and fibration, K-theory spectra (absent from both libraries), nonconnective K-theory and products. KTheoryLowDegrees' own targets are classical algebra - GL(A), K1, SK1, Steinitz, det : K0 -> Pic - and it touches higher K-theory only in its two comparison layers.

AutomorphicGaloisRepresentations' closure contains all but twenty-two stages of ArithmeticLocallySymmetricSpaces' and adds three hundred more: modular curves and Jacobians as schemes, Kuga-Sato varieties, etale cohomology with local systems, Eichler-Shimura, Weil-II purity, local Langlands for GL2, Hilbert modular varieties and the Fontaine functors. ArithmeticLocallySymmetricSpaces builds topological cohomology of arithmetic quotients - symmetric spaces, Borel-Serre, Hecke correspondences, duality - which is a prerequisite fragment of that.

CFSG's remaining theory is larger in bulk: the tripled-D4 carrier with group-level triality, the short-root G2 and F4 carriers as group schemes with their special isogenies in characteristic three and two (today only b2/g2/f4SpecialTorusEnd on the root datum exist), and all of L5, which imports the pinned Chevalley-Demazure group scheme over Z plus a per-family agreement MulEquiv. HopfRinow's remaining work is more deeply stacked - ODE smooth dependence and the geodesic flow, then exp_p, then normal neighbourhoods and the Gauss lemma and minimisation, then the TFAE, then the corollaries - but it is standard Riemannian geometry on a base where Layer 0 and the Levi-Civita/spray half of Layer 1 are already built.

SerreWeightAndLevelOptimisation needs Galois representations attached to modular and Hilbert modular forms - hence modular curves and Jacobians, etale cohomology, Eichler-Shimura, local Langlands and p-adic Hodge theory - plus integral Hecke modules and mod-p forms, finite flat group schemes, Neron models, and then Ribet, Mazur and Edixhoven, across fifty-one upstream roadmaps at depth seventeen. ArithmeticDynamics needs Berkovich geometry, polarized morphisms and heights, equidistribution and arboreal representations, across thirteen at depth six.

The two closures are nearly disjoint and comparably tall: ShimuraCompactifications' exclusive part is the Shimura/PEL/abelian-scheme moduli tower (ShimuraVarieties, ShimuraData, PELModuli, AlgebraicModuli), BorelRegulators' is the K-theory tower (KTheoryLowDegrees, GeneralAlgebraicKTheory, StableHomotopyKTheory, ArithmeticKTheory, MotivicEtaleKTheory) and it is the larger of the two. BorelRegulators also has to combine three independent unbuilt stacks - higher K-theory with finite generation, Borel-Serre and relative Lie-algebra cohomology with van Est, and the functional equation of zeta_F with Tamagawa measures - where ShimuraCompactifications extends a single one.

GeneralAlgebraicKTheory must build the whole of higher algebraic K-theory above the K_0 that Tau Ceti already has: the Q-construction, the plus construction, additivity, devissage, resolution and localisation, Waldhausen's S-construction with delooping and fibration, K-theory spectra (no stable-homotopy spectrum exists in either library), nonconnective theory and products - sixty upstream stages. ColemanIntegration needs the p-adic logarithm, annuli and residues, Frobenius lifts with rigid/de Rham cohomology on good-reduction curves, Coleman functions and polylogarithms, over twenty-one.
